title: 真实搭讪，搭讪大学生

timeline.summary: The male camera-holder says he is not selling something, asks for one woman's WeChat and says he wants to meet her. The burned subtitles clarify several phrases that the ASR garbles.
One woman and the camera-holder bring out phones and move them close together; the edit does not show enough device detail to prove that a contact was saved.
They discuss the many photographers nearby and the possibility of being mistaken for one. A woman responds that it is all right.
Phone handling continues briefly and the parties separate with an OK and goodbye; no later contact or outcome is shown.

claims.speaker: male_camera_holder_unconfirmed
claims.statement: The camera-holder opens by stating that he is not selling something, directly asks for one woman's WeChat and says he wants to meet her.
claims.conditions: This is an observed approach sequence, not evidence that the wording caused cooperation; the camera-holder is not independently authenticated as Mikey.

claims.speaker: woman_in_group_and_male_camera_holder
claims.statement: One woman participates in phone handling after the request and later says the photographer concern is not a problem.
claims.conditions: Participation in this moment does not establish informed consent to filming, attraction, a completed contact save or consent to later interaction.

examples.summary: A short public approach moves from an explicit contact request to phone handling, a brief photographer clarification and a goodbye.

speaker_attribution.speaker: male_camera_holder_unconfirmed
speaker_attribution.basis: Male speech aligns with first-person camera movement and an outstretched hand, but no reviewed frame independently identifies him as Mikey.

speaker_attribution.speaker: woman_in_group
speaker_attribution.basis: Two women are visible; sparse and one-second frames cannot map every short response to a specific woman with certainty.

visual_findings: All eight sampled frames and all twenty-three one-second dense frames were reviewed.
Two women are identifiable in a public shopping area; one appears to present or operate a phone during the exchange.
The phones' screens are not readable enough to verify a saved contact, and the edit ends after a goodbye.

permissions.reason: Distinct case only; identity, filming consent, completed exchange and downstream outcome are unverified.

limitations: The automatic transcript is garbled in S00002-S00006; burned subtitles support the broad sequence but were not treated as a word-for-word audio check.
The title calls the women university students, but neither the transcript nor the reviewed frames establish their student status.
Phone proximity and handling do not prove a successful WeChat exchange.
Visible faces create privacy risk; do not package identifiable imagery without privacy review.
One-second visual review is denser than the manifest sampling but is not continuous original audio-visual verification.
